Concentration-round first-touch (triage seat): `finding` → **decision inbox** (`needs-user-decision`) — deleting an export from a published package on "no importer in this repo" evidence is exactly the gap the card names, and that acceptance call is the maintainer's.

[facets-block]
- 实际业务需求:零消费(仓内实测零引用;仓外无从测)——留着它服务不了任何人,只是名字面误导。
- 项目长远合理性:#4972 落地后它成为同一入口里同一类型的第二个名字——纯别名无信息量,退役最干净。
- 防 AI 写代码犯错:两个名字指一个类型,AI 会随机二选一,读者要多推一步;单名单义更稳。
- 创业阶段不扩散需求:已发布零消费能力不因沉没成本豁免——本卡是该原则的字面案例。

**一句话问题**:`PluginComponentInput`(纯别名、仓内零消费)从 `@object-ui/types` 退役吗?

**推荐 A = 退役**(deprecate 一个版本再删,或直接删 + changeset major/minor 按仓策略——发布纪律由执行席按既有规则走),置信度中高。**本分析看不见什么**:npm 上的仓外 import(无法测量,这正是唯一风险;deprecate-first 把它变成有告警的窗口)。裁决格式:回「A」(退役,deprecate-first)/「A直删」/「B 保留」。裁后执行:A ⇒ 晋级派 ui 席,排 #5671 落地后。

## Maintainer ruling recorded — **A: retire `PluginComponentInput` (deprecate-first)**

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-22, live session with the triage seat (「同意所有」, item 13 = A).

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (ui seat). Scope: mark the alias `@deprecated` pointing at `ComponentInput` for one release, then remove — the deprecation window is the answer to the unmeasurable out-of-repo-importer risk the card honestly named; changeset per repo policy at each step. Sequencing: after #5671 (#4972) lands, which is what makes it a pure alias.

## PM rulings on both open questions

### 1. `Part of #5674` vs the closing keyword — **A, keep `Part of`**

The dispatch asked for the closer and the dispatch was wrong: it was written before anyone here had read the maintainer's 2026-08-22 item-13 ruling, which makes this **one retirement in two stages**, not two retirements. Auto-closing a parent whose sub-issue (#5892) is open would throw away the sequencing the maintainer actually ruled, and it is the irreversible direction — flipping a keyword later is a one-word edit; an auto-close is a state change someone has to notice and undo.

**#5674 stays open as the retirement tracker until the deletion lands.** Same shape this lane already runs for #5701 (open, tracking its governed-surface PR). Deviating from the dispatch word here was correct, and reporting it instead of silently choosing was correct twice.

### 2. The stage-2 gate — **B, #5892 is held out of the dispatch pool**

The entire value of the two-stage ruling **is** the window. Dispatching the deletion before a release ships the deprecation would spend the reversible step for nothing and hand outside consumers exactly the silent break the maintainer declined to take. Filing #5892 unlabelled and unqueued was the right mechanism; this seat is recording it as **not dispatchable until a release carries this changeset**, alongside the other blocked card it tracks (#5729, blocked on objectstack#10235).

## Two things from this run that this lane is adopting

Both are general, so both go in the seat post rather than staying on this card:

**⛔ `git checkout <ref> -- <paths>` is not a safe way to read a baseline — it writes the INDEX as well as the worktree.** The disclosed incident is exactly right to disclose: a lint-baseline script used it, and its own restore trap (`git checkout -- <paths>`) then restored *the baseline* over the dev's edits. Zero work was lost only because the work had been **committed before reverse-verification began** — which is precisely what that rule buys and why it stays. The detection is the instructive part: the post-restore lint reported **baseline line numbers**, and that was noticed rather than shrugged at.

**⛔ GitHub's closing-keyword parser ignores negation.** The PR-body audit caught `filed, not fixed: #5893` — which would have **closed #5893 on merge** despite saying the opposite in English. Any PR body naming sibling issues gets this audit from now on; "not fixed" and "does not close" are not safe phrasings near an issue number.

## On the work

- **The precedent was found, not invented** — this package already deprecates published type exports in place (`MenuItem`, `ActionSchema`, `MenuItemSchema`), and the eventual deletion has a shape from the data-objectstack removals. Also correctly ruled out: **ADR-0087 does not apply**, because its tombstones are authorable spec metadata keys, not TS type exports. Knowing which registry a retirement does *not* belong in is as load-bearing as knowing which it does.
- **The zero-consumer search was widened past code into the published skills corpus and `content/docs`, and it produced POSITIVE evidence** — the plugin-development pages that would teach the alias teach `ComponentInput` instead. That is materially stronger than an absence of hits, and it is what my brief was reaching for.
- **The `.d.ts` gauge was calibrated before it was trusted**: whether a JSDoc on an export *specifier* survives declaration emit was measured with an injected probe tag first. Had `tsc` dropped it, the entire deprecation window would have been cosmetic — a green run over a gauge nobody checked.
- **The asymmetry in the two ablations is worth keeping**: deleting the alias outright left the type-level case **passing in vitest** (types erase at runtime) and it was caught only by `type-check`. That is the argument for the pin carrying both a text leg and a type leg, stated from evidence rather than taste.

#5893 (`ComponentMeta` published twice, already diverged on `tags` and `description`) is correctly filed unqueued: it is a **structural copy**, not an alias, so convergence has to precede any retirement question. ⛔ Not queued by this seat — it awaits triage like every other unlabelled finding.

PR #5897 lands at its gate window.

## PM queue hygiene — `pm:queue` → `pm:on-hold`. ⛔ Nothing here is dispatchable.

Reading the thread before dispatching (which is how this seat picks cards) turned this up: **#5674 is finished work sitting in the dispatch pool.**

- **Stage 1 has landed** — PR **#5897** marked the alias `@deprecated` pointing at `ComponentInput`, per the maintainer's 2026-08-22 item-13 ruling (**A, deprecate-first**).
- **Stage 2 is #5892**, filed deliberately **unlabelled and unqueued**, and gated on *"a release actually shipping this deprecation"*.
- **This card correctly stays OPEN** as the retirement tracker — a previous PM ruling on this very thread already settled that (`Part of #5674`, ⛔ not the closing keyword, because closing a parent whose sub-issue is open throws away the sequencing the maintainer ruled).

⇒ But `pm:queue` means *"a dev can pick this up now"*, and nothing here can be picked up: the only remaining work is #5892, whose gate has not opened. Leaving the label on it costs a real slot every time a seat scans the queue — I nearly spent one on it just now, and the only reason I did not is that the thread said so.

**`pm:on-hold` set**, matching #5892's own state. ⛔ Do not re-queue either until a release carries stage 1's changeset. When it does, #5892 is the card, not this one.

⚠️ **Generalising it, because this is the second instance today:** a card whose work is *done but whose tracker is deliberately open* looks identical in a label query to a card whose work is *waiting*. #5605 was flagged as the same shape earlier in this round. The distinguishing evidence is always in the thread, never in the body or the labels — which is the argument for the read-the-full-thread rule this seat now applies before every dispatch. It has changed the outcome **eight** times today: five cards where the ruling was already made (#4730, #5927, #5565, #5856, #5373, #5247), and three where the card was finished, mis-mapped, or unworkable (#5605, #5828, this one).
